paragraphs: Resources Connection, Inc. ("RGP," the "Company," "we" or "us") is a global professional services firm based in Dallas, Texas (with offices worldwide) with three decades of experience helping the world's top organizations navigate change and seize opportunity. With three integrated offerings—On-Demand Talent, Consulting, and Outsourced Services—the Company provides CFOs and other C-suite leaders with the flexibility to solve today's most pressing challenges. The Company's principal markets of operations are North America, Europe & Asia Pacific.

The Company operates under the following business units: (i) On-Demand Talent, (ii) Consulting, (iii) Europe & Asia Pacific, (iv) Outsourced Services, and (v) Sitrick (disclosed as "All Other"). As noted below, we divested our Sitrick business on May 2, 2026.

We serve more than 1,500 clients around the world with approximately 3,000 professionals collectively engaged from 35 physical practice offices and multiple virtual offices. Headquartered in Dallas, Texas, we are proud to have served 90% of the Fortune 100 as of May 2026.
For fiscal 2026, the Company's operating segments were as follows:
•On-Demand Talent – provides businesses with a go-to source for bringing in experts when they need them, serving predominantly the office of the CFO.
•Consulting – drives transformation across people, processes and technology across domain areas including finance, technology and digital, risk and compliance and operational performance.
•Europe & Asia Pacific – a geographically defined segment that offers both on-demand and consulting services to clients throughout Europe and Asia Pacific.

•Outsourced Services – operating under the Countsy by RGPTM brand, this segment offers outsourced finance, accounting and human resource ("HR") services to startups, spinouts and scale-up enterprises, utilizing a technology platform and fractional team.
•Sitrick – a crisis communications and public relations firm that provides corporate, financial, transactional and crisis communication and management services.

On April 7, 2026, the Company entered into a Membership Interest Purchase Agreement (the "Purchase Agreement") with Sitrick Group, LLC ("Sitrick") and Sitrick, LLC (the "Buyer"), pursuant to which the Company agreed to sell 100% of the membership interests of Sitrick to the Buyer. The sale was completed on May 2, 2026. As a result of the sale of Sitrick, the "All Other" segment was eliminated as of May 30, 2026. See Note 3 – Acquisitions and Dispositions in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements included herein under "Item 8., Financial Statements and Supplemental Data" for further discussion.

Our services respond to what we believe is a permanent marketplace shift: namely, organizations are increasingly choosing to address their workforce needs in more flexible ways. Permanent professional personnel positions are being reduced as organizations engage agile talent for project initiatives and transformation work.

Organizations use a mix of alternative resources to execute initiatives and projects. Some companies rely solely on their own employees who may lack the requisite time, experience or skills for specific projects. Other companies may outsource entire projects to consulting firms, which provides them access to the expertise of the firm but often entails significant cost, insufficient management control of the project and a lack of ultimate ownership at project completion. As a more cost-efficient alternative, companies sometimes use temporary employees from traditional and internet-based staffing

firms, although these employees may be less experienced or less qualified than employees from professional services firms. Finally, companies can execute initiatives and projects by leveraging professional services firms like RGP to fill resource or skills gap or provide end-to-end outcome-based solutions. The use of project consultants as a viable alternative to traditional accounting, consulting, and law firms allows companies to:
•Strategically access specialized skills and expertise for projects of set durations; •Engage the very best expert talent across regions and geographies;

headings: Risks Related to the Business Environment
An economic downturn or deterioration of general macroeconomic conditions could continue to adversely affect our global operations and financial condition.
The market for professional services is highly competitive, and if we are unable to compete effectively against our competitors, our business and operating results could be adversely affected.
Events affecting financial institutions could adversely affect our and our clients' liquidity and financial performance.
Risks Related to Human Capital Resources
Our business could suffer if we lose the services of one or more key members of our senior management or key sales professionals.
Significant increases in wages or payroll-related costs could have a material adverse effect on our financial results.

We may be unable to adequately meet the needs of our clients with our consultants, which can harm our reputation, affect our ability to win new business and have a material adverse effect on our financial results.
Risks Related to Our Business Operations and Initiatives
Our business depends upon our ability to secure new projects from clients and renew expired contracts, and we could be adversely affected if we fail to do so.
Our financial results could suffer if we are unable to achieve or maintain a suitable pay/bill ratio.

We derive significant revenue and profits from contracts awarded through a competitive bidding process, which can impose substantial costs on us, and we will lose revenue and profits if we fail to compete effectively.
Our contracts may contain provisions that are unfavorable to us and permit our clients to, among other things, terminate our contracts partially or completely at any time prior to completion.

We may be unable to realize the level of the anticipated benefits that we expect from our transformation and restructuring initiatives, which may adversely impact our business and results of operations.
Our digital expansion and technology transformation efforts may not be successful, which could adversely impact our growth and profitability.
We may not be able to build an efficient support structure as our business continues to grow and transform.
We may not be able to grow our business, manage our growth or sustain our current business.
Our ability to serve clients internationally is integral to our strategy and our international activities expose us to additional operational challenges we might not otherwise face.
We have acquired, and may continue to acquire, companies, and these acquisitions could disrupt our business.
We may be unable to adequately protect our intellectual property rights, including our brand name.
Risks Related to AI, Information Technology, Cybersecurity and Data Protection
Our computer hardware and software and telecommunications systems are susceptible to damage, breach or interruption.
Legal and Regulatory Risks
Failure to comply with data privacy laws and regulations could have a materially adverse effect on our reputation, results of operations or financial condition, or have other adverse consequences.
We may be legally liable for damages resulting from the actions of our employees, the performance of projects by our consultants or for our clients' mistreatment of our personnel.
Changes in applicable tax laws or adverse results in tax audits or interpretations could have a material adverse effect on our business and operating results.
paragraphs: The risks described below should be considered carefully before a decision to buy shares of our common stock is made. The order of the risks is not an indication of their relative weight or importance. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones facing us but do represent those risks and uncertainties we believe are material to us. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also adversely impact and impair our business. If any of the following risks actually occur, our business could be harmed. In that case, the trading price of our common stock could decline, and all or part of the investment in our common stock might be lost. When determining whether to buy our common stock, other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our financial statements and the related notes, should also be reviewed.

We are exposed to the risk of an economic downturn or deterioration of general macroeconomic conditions, including slower growth or recession, inflation, or decreases in consumer spending power or confidence, which has had and could continue to have a significant impact on our business, financial condition, and results of operations. Recent inflationary conditions and the continue elevation of high interest rates, geopolitical conflicts as further discussed below and increasing diplomatic and trade friction, including as a result of new and increased tariffs imposed by the U.S. against China, Mexico, Canada and other countries, pandemics or public health crises, have caused disruptions in the U.S. and global economy, and uncertainty regarding general economic conditions within some regions and countries in which we operate, including concerns about a potential U.S. and/or global recession. These disruptions and uncertainties have led, and may continue to lead, to reluctance on the part of some companies to spend on discretionary projects. Deterioration of or prolonged uncertainty related to the global economy or tightening credit markets, including as a result of trade friction or other geopolitical uncertainty, could cause some of our clients, particularly those reliant on global supply chains, to experience liquidity problems or other financial difficulties and could further reduce the demand for our services and adversely affect our business in the future.

Geopolitical instability, including the conflict and unrest in the Middle East, could continue to create global economic and market uncertainty in a manner that could adversely affect our operations. Such conflicts and instability divert international trade and capital flows, disrupt global supply chains, delay companies' investment and hiring and erode consumer confidence, and periods of elevated geopolitical risks have historically been associated with negative effects on global economic activity. Although none of our operations are in areas of the Middle East experiencing conflict, the continuation or further escalation of geopolitical tensions, or future instances of political unrest in other geographies, could impact other markets where we do business, including Europe and Asia Pacific, or cause negative global economic effects which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

Economic deterioration at one or more of our clients may also affect our allowance for credit losses and collectability of accounts receivable. Our estimate of losses resulting from our clients' failure to make required payments for services rendered has historically been within our expectations and the provisions established. While our overall receivable collections have not been severely impacted by the softening economy or other geopolitical events, we cannot guarantee we will continue to experience the same credit loss rates we have in the past. A significant change in the liquidity or financial position of our clients could cause unfavorable trends in receivable collections and cash flows and additional allowances for anticipated losses may be required. These additional allowances could materially affect our future financial results.

In addition, we are required periodically, and at least annually, to assess the recoverability of certain assets, including deferred tax assets, long-lived assets and goodwill. Downturns in the U.S. and international economies have in the past, and could in the future, adversely affect our evaluation of the recoverability of deferred tax assets, long-lived assets and goodwill. Although the additional tax valuation allowances and the impairment of long-lived assets and goodwill are non-cash expenses, they could materially affect our future financial results and financial condition.

Resources Global Professionals ("RGP," "we" or "us") is a global professional services firm based in Dallas, Texas (with offices worldwide) with three decades of experience helping the world's top organizations navigate change and seize opportunity. With three integrated offerings — On-Demand Talent, Consulting, and Outsourced Services — we provide CFOs and other C-suite leaders with the flexibility to solve today's most pressing challenges. The Company's principal markets of operations are North America, Europe & Asia Pacific.

We operate under the following reporting units: (i) On-Demand Talent, (ii) Consulting, (iii) Europe & Asia Pacific, and (iv) Outsourced Services. Our previous reportable segments included Sitrick, a crisis communications and public relations firm, which did not individually meet the quantitative thresholds to qualify as a reportable segment (disclosed as "All Other"). On May 2, 2026, we completed the sale of 100% of the membership interests of Sitrick Group, LLC ("Sitrick"), to Sitrick, LLC, an entity owned by one of the original founders of Sitrick Group, LLC. The Company initiated the sale in connection with its broader transformation initiative to simplify its business portfolio..As a result of the sale of Sitrick, the All Other segment was eliminated as of May 30, 2026. The Company has presented the results of the All Other segment through the date the sale was completed for the year ended May 30, 2026. Following the sale, the Company received no new income from Sitrick, other than rent payments on sub-leased office buildings, and had no further involvement or continuing influence over its operations.
In fiscal 2026, we focused and executed upon the following enterprise growth drivers: •Expand cross-sell opportunities through our diversified services platform;
•Scale our high-value Consulting solutions and refocus On-Demand Talent offerings to address the evolving needs of our clients;
•Drive improvement in cost structure, simplify and optimize our business portfolio; and
•Further leverage value-based pricing to improve profitability.

Expand cross-sell opportunities through our diversified services platform – We offer a unique blend of services in On-Demand Talent, Consulting, and Outsourced Services, enabling high flexibility and high impact solutions for enterprises worldwide. This unique model is designed to meet clients' evolving needs in a disrupted business environment. Our Consulting capability provides us with deeper visibility into our clients' transformation agendas to drive greater opportunities for our On-Demand execution capabilities, while our agile talent base within our On-Demand business provides greater financial flexibility and better skill set alignment for our Consulting business. In our Outsourced Services business, we have and will continue to expand Countsy's total addressable market beyond the start-up ecosystem to serve the finance, accounting and human resources needs surrounding spin-outs and carve-outs. In fiscal 2026, we made progress in broadening client relationships by cross-selling across our diversified service offerings and introducing complementary solutions as client needs evolve. We believe this will continue to enable us to deepen our partnerships with CFOs and other C-suite business leaders, strengthen client retention, and increase wallet share while positioning the Company as a long-term, trusted partner for transformation and performance improvement.

Scale our high-value Consulting solutions and refocus On-Demand offerings to address the evolving needs of our clients – In a volatile and rapidly shifting global economic environment, CFOs and business leaders need partners who combine expertise with flexibility. We continue to build strong relationships with C-suite leaders, to support their organizations' transformation journeys with specialized on-demand expertise, high-value consulting, and integrated outsourced delivery. In fiscal 2026, we completed the integration of our consulting assets including Reference Point LLC

("Reference Point") into one cohesive consulting business unit. In addition, we have made focused investments to bring more sales capacity and depth to the consulting team and to further expand our service capabilities in Mergers and Acquisitions, Data Analytics and artificial intelligence ("AI"). Our core solutions are: enterprise resource planning ("ERP") and cloud finance systems modernization, financial planning and analysis enhancement, accounting close process optimization, SEC compliance, post acquisitions integration, enterprise risk management, data strategy and analytics, AI adoption and enterprise digital transformation. Concurrent to evolving our solutions to meet market demand, we have also made progress to evolve our talent strategy to modernize and refresh the skillsets within our consultant base, both bench and agile, to serve our clients across On-Demand or Consulting engagements, particularly in the area of technology and AI fluency.

Drive improvement in cost structure, simplify and optimize our business portfolio – As we execute strategic initiatives to improve our topline, we have also prioritized reducing our cost structure and maintaining ongoing cost discipline to deliver improved profitability. In fiscal 2026, we performed a comprehensive review of our operating model to redesign and streamline our cost structure, including simplification of business processes. In connection with this effort, we completed two workforce reductions affecting management and administrative roles improving our annual selling, general and administrative expenses ("SG&A") by $12.0 million to $14.0 million. In addition, as the result of our business portfolio review, we completed the sale of Sitrick in May 2026. Finally, we continue to improve the functionalities and user adoption of our recently implemented technology to achieve further operating efficiencies.

Further leverage value-based pricing – Building on the progress we made in previous fiscal years, we continued to advance our value-based pricing strategy to improve bill rates and pricing leverage, particularly in the Consulting business, as we pursue larger-scale, higher-value engagements that deliver measurable impact for clients.

Effective November 3, 2025, Roger Carlile, a director of the Company, was appointed as the Company's President and Chief Executive Officer ("CEO"). In connection with his appointment, the Company entered into an employment agreement with Mr. Carlile with a term that extends through November 3, 2028 and will automatically renew annually thereafter. In October 2025, the Company's Board of Directors elected not to renew the "Period of Employment" under the Company's existing Employment Agreement, dated February 3, 2020 and as subsequently amended, with Kate W. Duchene, the Company's former President and CEO. Ms. Duchene stepped down as the Company's President and CEO, and as a member of the Board, on November 2, 2025. She served as an Executive Advisor through January 3, 2026 to assist the Company and Mr. Carlile with the continuity of leadership. See Note 1 – Description of the Company and its Business in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements included in Part II, Item 8 "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for additional information regarding the severance benefits paid to Ms. Duchene.

On March 3, 2026, the Company entered into a Separation and General Release Agreement with Bhadreskumar Patel, the Company's Chief Operating Officer ("COO"), that provided the last day of Mr. Patel's employment by the Company would be May 15, 2026. See Note 1 – Description of the Company and its Business in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements included in Part II, Item 8 "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for additional information regarding the severance benefits paid to Mr. Patel.

paragraphs: Resources Connection, Inc. ("RGP," the "Company," "we" or "us") 為一間全球專業服務公司，總部設於德州達拉斯（全球多處設有辦公室），擁有三十年經驗，協助世界頂級企業應對變革並把握機會。透過三大整合性服務項目—On-Demand Talent、Consulting 與 Outsourced Services，本公司為財務長（CFO）及其他高階主管提供靈活性，以解決當前最迫切的挑戰。本公司主要營運市場為北美、歐洲及亞太地區。
本公司營運以下業務單位：(i) On-Demand Talent、(ii) Consulting、(iii) 歐洲及亞太地區、(iv) Outsourced Services，以及 (v) Sitrick（披露為 "All Other"）。如下列所說明，我們於 2026 年 5 月 2 日已出售 Sitrick 事業。
我們服務全球超過 1,500 家客戶，約有 3,000 名專業人員透過 35 處實體辦公室及多處虛擬辦公室共同參與。總部設於德州達拉斯，我們為截至 2026 年 5 月的財富 100 大企業中 90% 提供服務。
2026 年會計年度，本公司營運分部如下：
•On-Demand Talent – 提供企業一個即時取得專家的來源，主要服務財務長辦公室。
•Consulting – 帶動在財務、科技與數位、風險與合規及營運績效等領域的人力、流程與科技的轉型。
•歐洲及亞太地區 – 一個以地理為基礎的分部，為歐洲及亞太地區的客戶提供即時服務與諮詢服務。
•Outsourced Services – 以 Countsy by RGPTM 品牌營運，此分部為新創公司、衍生公司及擴張型企業提供外包財務、會計及人力資源（"HR"）服務，運用科技平台與分數團隊。
•Sitrick – 一間危機溝通與公共關係公司，提供企業、財務、交易及危機溝通與管理服務。

於 2026 年 4 月 7 日，本公司與 Sitrick Group, LLC（"Sitrick"）及 Sitrick, LLC（"Buyer"）簽訂會員權益買賣協議（"Purchase Agreement"），根據協議，本公司同意將 Sitrick 全部會員權益出售給 Buyer。該交易於 2026 年 5 月 2 日完成。由於 Sitrick 的出售，自 2026 年 5 月 30 日起，"All Other" 分部被取消。有關進一步討論，請參見本文件 "Item 8., 財務報表與補充資料" 所包含的會計師備註第 3 項 – 收購與處分。
我們的服務回應我們認為市場永久性變革：即，機構越來越傾向以更靈活的方式處理其人力需求。機構正在減少永久性專業人員職位，並聘請敏捷人才進行專案計畫與轉型工作。

機構使用多種替代性資源來執行計畫與專案。有些公司僅依靠自己的員工，這些員工可能缺乏執行特定專案所需的時間、經驗或技能。其他公司則可能將整個專案委外給顧問公司，這可讓他們取得該公司的專業知識，但通常會產生顯著的成本、對專案的管理控制不足，以及在專案完成時缺乏最終的所有權。作為更節省成本的替代方案，公司有時會使用來自傳統及基於互聯網的人力派遣機構的臨時員工，儘管這些員工可能不如來自專業服務機構的員工那麼有經驗或具備資格。最後，公司可以透過利用專業服務機構如 RGP 來彌補資源或技能缺口，或提供端到端的結果導向解決方案來執行計畫與專案。使用專案顧問作為傳統會計、顧問及律師事務所的可行替代方案，使公司得以：
• 戰略性地取得特定期間專案所需的專業技能與知識；• 聘請各區域及地理區域內最優秀的專家人才；
• 戰略性地取得特定期間專案所需的專業技能與知識；• 聘請各區域及地理區域內最優秀的專家人才；

paragraphs: 以下對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，應與我們的財務報表及其相關附註一併閱讀。此討論與分析包含前瞻性陳述，涉及風險與不確定性。我們的實際結果可能與這些前瞻性陳述所預期的有重大差異，原因包括但不限於在本年度報告表 10-K 第 I 項第 1A 項「風險因素」及本年度報告表其他地方所討論的某些因素。請參閱上方「前瞻性陳述」以取得進一步說明。

Resources Global Professionals（"RGP," "我們"或"我們公司"）是一家全球專業服務公司，總部設於德克薩斯州達拉斯（全球各處均有辦事處），擁有三 decades 的經驗，協助世界頂級企業應對變革並把握機會。透過三個整合的服務方案—On-Demand Talent、Consulting 與 Outsourced Services—我們為財務長（CFO）及其他高階主管提供靈活性，以解決當前最迫切的挑戰。本公司主要營運市場為北美、歐洲及亞太地區。

我們的營運單位如下：(i) On-Demand Talent、(ii) Consulting、(iii) 歐洲及亞太地區、(iv) Outsourced Services。我們先前的應報告分部包括 Sitrick，這是一家危機溝通與公共關係公司，但該分部未達成量化門檻，因此不具備應報告分部資格（披露為 "All Other"）。2026 年 5 月 2 日，我們完成了將 Sitrick Group, LLC（"Sitrick"）100% 會員權益出售給 Sitrick, LLC（一家由 Sitrick Group, LLC 原創創始人所擁有之實體）。本公司啟動此交易，係因應其更廣泛的轉型計畫，以簡化其業務組合。由於 Sitrick 的出售，自 2026 年 5 月 30 日起，All Other 分部已刪除。本公司已於 2026 年 5 月 30 日結束的財務年度內，披露 All Other 分部的結果。交易後，本公司自 Sitrick 無新增收入，僅有子租賃辦公大樓的租金收入，且對其營運無進一步參與或持續影響。
2026 年會計年度，我們專注並執行以下企業成長動力：•透過我們多元化的服務平台擴大交叉銷售機會；
•擴大我們高價值 Consulting 解決方案，並重新聚焦 On-Demand Talent 提供方案，以應對客戶需求的變化；
•推動成本結構改善，簡化並優化我們的業務組合；以及
•進一步運用價值導向定價，以提高利潤率。

透過我們多元化的服務平台擴大交叉銷售機會—我們在 On-Demand Talent、Consulting 與 Outsourced Services 提供獨特的服務組合，為全球企業提供高靈活性與高影響力的解決方案。此獨特模式旨在應對受幹擾的商業環境中客戶的變革需求。我們的 Consulting 能力使我們能更深入瞭解客戶的轉型計畫，以推動我們 On-Demand 執行能力的更大機會，而我們 On-Demand 事業中的靈活人才庫則為我們 Consulting 事業提供更高的財務靈活性與更好的技能對應。在 Outsourced Services 事業中，我們已並會持續擴展 Countsy 的總可接觸市場，超越創始生態系，以服務分拆（spin-outs）與切割（carve-outs）周圍的財務、會計與人力資源需求。在 2026 年會計年度，我們在擴大客戶關係方面取得進展，透過交叉銷售我們多元化的服務方案，並根據客戶需求的變化引入補充解決方案。我們相信這將持續使我們能深化與財務長（CFO）及其他高階主管的夥伴關係，強化客戶留存，並提高客戶支出佔比，同時將本公司定位為長期受信賴的轉型與績效改善夥伴。

擴展我們高價值的諮詢解決方案，並重新聚焦於即時服務方案，以回應客戶不斷變化的需求 – 在一個波動且快速變化的全球經濟環境中，財務長與企業領導者需要兼具專業知識與靈活性的夥伴。我們持續與執行長級領導者建立強大關係，以專門的即時服務專業知識、高價值諮詢服務以及整合的委外交付方式，支持其組織的轉型旅程。在會計年度 2026 年，我們完成了將諮詢資產包括 Reference Point LLC（"Reference Point"）整合為一個協調的諮詢業務單位。此外，我們已針對增加諮詢團隊的銷售能力與深度，以及進一步擴展我們在併購、數據分析及人工智慧（"AI"）領域的服務能力，進行專注投資。我們的核心解決方案為：企業資源規劃（"ERP"）與雲端財務系統現代化、財務規劃與分析增強、會計結賬流程優化、證券交易委員會（SEC）合規、併購後整合、企業風險管理、數據策略與分析、人工智慧採用與企業數位轉型。同時，隨著我們調整解決方案以符合市場需求，我們也已取得進展，以現代化並更新我們諮詢團隊（包括固定與敏捷團隊）的技能組合，以服務客戶在即時服務或諮詢合作中的需求，特別是在科技與人工智慧專業能力方面。

推動成本結構改善，簡化並優化我們的業務組合 – 隨著我們執行戰略性計畫以改善營收，我們同時也優先考量降低成本結構並維持持續的成本紀律，以實現改善利潤率。在會計年度 2026 年，我們進行了對營運模式的全面檢視，以重新設計並簡化成本結構，包括簡化業務流程。配合此項努力，我們完成了兩次人力精簡，影響管理與行政職務，使我們的年度銷售、一般及行政費用（"SG&A"）減少 12.0 百萬美元至 14.0 百萬美元。此外，根據我們的業務組合檢視結果，我們於 2026 年 5 月完成了 Sitrick 的出售。最後，我們持續改善近期實施的科技功能與用戶採用率，以實現進一步的營運效率。

推動成本結構改善，簡化並優化我們的業務組合 – 隨著我們執行戰略性計畫以改善營收，我們同時也優先考量降低成本結構並維持持續的成本紀律，以實現改善利潤率。在會計年度 2026 年，我們進行了對營運模式的全面檢視，以重新設計並簡化成本結構，包括簡化業務流程。配合此項努力，我們完成了兩次人力精簡，影響管理與行政職務，使我們的年度銷售、一般及行政費用（"SG&A"）減少 12.0 百萬美元至 14.0 百萬美元。此外，根據我們的業務組合檢視結果，我們於 2026 年 5 月完成了 Sitrick 的出售。最後，我們持續改善近期實施的科技功能與用戶採用率，以實現進一步的營運效率。
進一步強化以價值為基礎的定價策略 – 延續前會計年度所取得的進展，本公司持續推動以價值為基礎的定價策略，以提升諮詢業務的收費率與定價彈性，特別是在追求規模更大、價值更高的專案，以為客戶帶來可衡量的影響方面。

自2025年11月3日起，Roger Carlile，本公司董事，被任命為本公司總裁及首席執行官（"CEO"）。配合此任命，本公司與Mr. Carlile簽訂了聘僱契約，契約期間至2028年11月3日為止，並於之後每年自動續約。2025年10月，本公司董事會決定不續約本公司現有聘僱契約，該契約簽訂於2020年2月3日，並經後續修正，與Kate W. Duchene，本公司前總裁及首席執行官的聘僱期間。Ms. Duchene於2025年11月2日辭去本公司總裁及首席執行官職務，並離開董事會。她於2026年1月3日擔任執行顧問，協助本公司與Mr. Carlile實現領導層的順利過渡。有關Ms. Duchene所獲得的離職補償金額，請參閱本年度10-K申報表第二部分第8項「財務資料與補充資料」所附的財務會計摘要中「第1項 – 本公司及其業務之說明」。
2026年3月3日，本公司與Bhadreskumar Patel，本公司首席運營官（"COO"）簽訂了離職與一般釋放協議，該協議規定Mr. Patel在本公司最後工作日為2026年5月15日。有關Mr. Patel所獲得的離職補償金額，請參閱本年度10-K申報表第二部分第8項「財務資料與補充資料」所附的財務會計摘要中「第1項 – 本公司及其業務之說明」。

headings: 與業務環境相關的風險
經濟衰退或總體經濟條件惡化可能持續不利影響我們的全球營運與財務狀況。
專業服務市場競爭激烈，若我們無法有效與競爭對手競爭，將可能不利影響我們的業務與營運結果。
影響金融機構的事件可能不利影響我們與我們客戶的流動性與財務表現。
與人力資本資源相關的風險
若我們失去一位或多位高階管理階層或關鍵銷售專業人員的服務，將可能影響我們的業務。
工資或 payroll 相關成本顯著增加，可能對我們的財務結果產生重大不利影響。
我們可能無法充分滿足客戶的需求，這可能損害我們的聲譽，影響我們獲得新業務的能力，並對我們的財務結果產生重大不利影響。
與我們業務運作及策略相關之風險
我們之業務依賴我們能否從客戶取得新項目並續約到期合約，若我們未能做到，可能會對我們造成不利影響。
若我們無法達成或維持合適之應收帳款/應計收入比率，我們之財務結果可能會受影響。
我們從競標過程取得之合約中獲取顯著之營業收入與利潤，此過程可能對我們造成重大成本負擔，若我們未能有效競爭，將會導致收入與利潤流失。
我們之合約可能包含對我們不利之條款，允許客戶在合約完成前，隨時部分或完全終止合約。
我們可能無法實現預期自轉型與重整策略中所獲得之效益，此可能會對我們之業務與營運結果造成不利影響。
我們之數位擴張與科技轉型努力可能無法成功，此可能會對我們之成長與獲利能力造成不利影響。
我們可能無法建立高效之支援架構，以因應業務持續成長與轉型之需求。
我們可能無法擴大業務規模、管理業務成長或維持目前的業務狀況。
我們服務國際客戶的能力是我們策略的重要組成部分，而國際業務活動使我們面臨額外的運營挑戰，這些挑戰我們在國內業務中可能不會遇到。
我們已取得，且可能持續取得公司，這些併購行為可能幹擾我們的業務。
我們可能無法充分保護我們的智慧財產權，包括我們的品牌名稱。
與人工智慧、資訊科技、網路安全及資料保護相關的風險
我們的電腦硬體與軟體及電信系統可能遭受損壞、入侵或中斷。
法律與法規相關的風險
未能遵守資料隱私權法律與法規可能對我們的聲譽、營運結果或財務狀況造成重大不利影響，或產生其他不利後果。
本公司可能因員工行為、顧問執行專案之表現，或客戶對本公司人員之不當對待而產生損害賠償責任。
適用稅法之變更或稅務稽查結果不利或解釋，可能對本公司營運及營業成果產生重大不利影響。
paragraphs: 下列風險應在決定是否購買本公司普通股之前謹慎考慮。風險的順序並不代表其相對重要性。下列所述的風險與不確定性並非本公司唯一面臨的風險，但確實代表我們認為對本公司重要的風險與不確定性。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前尚未為本公司所知或目前認為不重要，也可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。若任何下列風險實際發生，將可能對本公司業務造成損害。在此情況下，本公司普通股的交易價格可能下跌，投資人投資於本公司普通股的全部或部分金額可能喪失。在決定是否購買本公司普通股時，也應審閱本年度報告表10-K中其他資訊，包括財務報表及其相關附註。

本公司面臨經濟衰退或總體經濟條件惡化風險，包括成長放緩或經濟衰退、通貨膨脹，或消費者支出能力或信心下降，這些因素已對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運成果造成重大影響，並可能持續造成影響。近期通貨膨脹情況與高利率持續升高、如後文所述的國際政治衝突，以及日益增加的外交與貿易摩擦，包括因美國對中國、墨西哥、加拿大及其他國家所施加的新增或提高關稅所致，以及疫情或公共衛生危機，已造成美國與全球經濟的幹擾，並對本公司營運地區與國家的總體經濟條件產生不確定性，包括對美國與/或全球經濟衰退的擔憂。這些幹擾與不確定性已導致，並可能持續導致，部分公司對進行非必要投資的謹慎態度。全球經濟或信貸市場的惡化或持續不確定性，包括因貿易摩擦或其他國際政治不確定性所致，可能導致部分客戶，特別是依賴全球供應鏈的客戶，遭遇流動性問題或其他財務困難，並可能進一步減少對本公司服務的需求，對本公司未來業務造成不利影響。

國際政治不穩定，包括中東地區的衝突與動亂，可能持續造成全球經濟與市場的不確定性，並可能對本公司營運造成不利影響。這些衝突與不穩定會干擾國際貿易與資金流動，幹擾全球供應鏈，延宕企業的投資與僱用，並削弱消費者信心。歷史上，國際政治風險升高期間，通常與全球經濟活動的負面影響有關。儘管本公司在中東地區未有營運，但國際政治緊張情勢的持續或進一步升級，或未來其他地區的政治動亂，可能影響本公司營運的市場，包括歐洲與亞太地區，或造成負面的全球經濟影響，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運成果造成不利影響。

本公司客戶的經濟狀況惡化也可能影響本公司對信用減損的提列與應收帳款的可收回性。本公司對客戶未能支付所提供服務的損失預估，歷來均在預期範圍內，並已建立相關提列。儘管本公司整體應收帳款的回收情況未因經濟放緩或其他國際政治事件而受到嚴重影響，但本公司無法保證未來將持續維持過去的信用減損率。本公司客戶的流動性或財務狀況的重大變動，可能導致應收帳款回收與現金流出現不利趨勢，並可能需要增加預計損失的提列。這些額外提列可能對本公司未來財務結果產生重大影響。
此外，本公司定期，至少每年，必須評估某些資產的可收回性，包括遞延所得稅資產、長期資產與商譽。美國與國際經濟的衰退，過去曾對本公司評估遞延所得稅資產、長期資產與商譽的可收回性造成影響，未來也可能造成影響。雖然額外的所得稅價值減損與長期資產與商譽的減損為非現金費用，但這些費用可能對本公司未來財務結果與財務狀況產生重大影響。
本公司營運於一個競爭激烈且分散的市場，與多種提供類似服務的組織競爭客戶與顧問。本公司主要競爭對手包括：諮詢公司；地方、區域、國家與國際會計及其他傳統專業服務公司；獨立承包商；傳統與網際網路
